description: `cli-health status` reports Ollama and Qdrant availability plus the count of currently indexed commands.

requirements.description: The `cli-health status` command must report: (1) Ollama availability (reachable / unreachable) including the base URL checked; (2) Qdrant availability (reachable / unreachable) including the base URL checked; (3) the total count of currently indexed commands in the Qdrant collection. The command must respond within 3 seconds under normal conditions and must exit with code 0 regardless of dependency availability (status is informational, not a health gate).
requirements.title: Dependency Status Reporting

validation.notes: Given a mocked Ollama HTTP client returning 200, status reports Ollama as reachable
Given a mocked Ollama HTTP client returning connection refused, status reports Ollama as unreachable
Given a mocked Qdrant client returning collection info with 42 vectors, status reports indexed count as 42
Given both dependencies unreachable, status exits with code 0
Run `cli-health status` with real Qdrant and Ollama running after a reindex; assert reported count matches the number of commands in the indexed manifests
Run `cli-health status` with Qdrant stopped; assert output contains unreachable indicator and exit code is 0
`cli-health status` must return output within 3 seconds on a local stack regardless of dependency state (timeouts must be bounded to enforce this)
Operators can quickly confirm AI search infrastructure readiness before debugging search quality issues

title: Dependency status reporting
